questions.question_text: Catastrophic reaction is best described as a/an

options.text: Hysterical reaction to stressors seen in anxiety states
Response to cognitive challenge seen in patients with dementia.
Response to traumatic recall seen in patients with PTSD

correct_answer.text: Response to cognitive challenge seen in patients with dementia.

questions.explanation:
This is a response occasionally seen in patients with dementia. When patients with dementia are asked to perform beyond their, now
impaired, performance level, there is sudden agitation, anger and occasional violence, which is called a catastrophic reaction (Goldstein).

questions.question_text:
Mr X is a 27-year-old gentleman admitted to a psychiatric unit for treatment of his psychotic illness. His mental state �uctuates in that on
one occasion he is restless, agitated and excited and on another occasion he is mute, immobile and also demonstrates Waxy �exibility.
Which of the following medicationa is most likely to help him?
questions.explanation:
This gentleman has catatonia alternating between excitement and stupor. This could be a feature of catatonic schizophrenia in which the
onset is usually acute, the course is usually episodic and recovery from the episode is usually complete. However, residual features are
present after 2 or more episodes. Catatonia could respond to benzodiazepines such as lorazepam and improvements have been achieved in
case studies dramatically, although only temporarily.

questions.question_text: What is the proportion of individuals with epilepsy that commit suicide?
questions.explanation: This elevated risk is seen even in the absence of diagnosable depression.

questions.question_text: The estimate of lifetime suicide prevalence in schizophrenia patients observed either from �rst admission or illness onset is
questions.explanation:
The suicide rate in schizophrenia was thought to be 10% for a long time But a recent meta-analysis which included studies that were
continued for at least 2 years with minimum 90% follow-up rates concluded di�erently (Palmer, Arch Gen Psych 2005). The estimate of
lifetime suicide prevalence in those observed from �rst admission or illness onset was 5.6% (95% con�dence interval, 3.7%-8.5%).

questions.question_text: The rates of completed suicide are signi�cantly raised in all mental disorders except
questions.explanation:
The rates of completed suicide are signi�cantly raised in all mental disorders excepting mental handicap and dementia. Studies examining
completed suicides in patients with mental illness show inadequate doses of therapeutic drug treatment, increased drop-out rate from
follow-up, and increased presence of untreated co morbidity.

questions.question_text: The most common psychiatric diagnosis associated with suicide is
questions.explanation: The most common psychiatric diagnoses in suicide are major depression (30-31%) and alcohol dependence (17-24%).

questions.question_text: Most countries have a higher male suicide rates than female suicide rates. This is not the case in
questions.explanation:
The male: female ratio is 3.5:1 for completed suicides globally. An exception is China where females have higher or comparable rates to
males. Number of suicides in China is 30% greater than that of whole Europe - due to the size of the population.

questions.question_text:
According to the survey of psychiatric morbidities among adults living in private households, the lifetime prevalence of deliberate self harm
in patients with a possible psychotic disorder is
questions.explanation: The lifetime prevalence of DSH in patients with a possible psychotic disorder is 25% (ONS statistics, 2007).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding suicide in bipolar disorder is false?

options.text: Suicide rates are 15 times higher than general population
Most bipolar patients succeed in suicide attempts when manic.
Suicide rates are higher than unipolar depression

correct_answer.text: Most bipolar patients succeed in suicide attempts when manic.

questions.explanation:
Suicide rates in people with bipolar disorder are estimated to be around 10% - 19%. This is 15 times that of the general population. At least a
quarter will attempt suicide. This is higher than that seen in unipolar depression. The depressed phase of bipolar disorder is linked to about
80% of suicide attempts and completed suicides. Mortality rates from natural causes (mainly vascular disease) are also increased in people
with bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: What is the risk of suicide in a patient with schizophrenia (expressed in percentage)?
questions.explanation:
Suicide claims the lives of about 6% of schizophrenic patients. They are more likely to injure themselves than others. Between 2% and 12%
of all individuals dying by suicide have schizophrenia. (Heila et al 1997).

questions.question_text: The prevalence of suicidal ideations in the past year among school-going adolescent in Britain is
questions.explanation:
Suicidal ideation (without deliberate self harm) in the past year was reported by 15.0% of an adolescent cohort in UK (school pupils - self
report). This was more common in females (22%) than males (8.5%) (Odds ratio 3.1).

questions.question_text: Which of the following diagnoses is associated with an increased risk of suicide?
questions.explanation:
Some patients with schizophrenia develop depressive features within 12 months of an acute episode of psychosis. The depressive features
develop in the presence of residual or active features of schizophrenia and are associated with an increased risk of suicide. It may be di�cult
to di�erentiate from negative symptoms or Parkinsonism and is associated with an increased risk of suicide.

questions.question_text: What is the risk of suicide in the next year for a patient who has deliberately self-harmed today?
questions.explanation:
Risk of suicide within one year of DSH - 0.7% (nearly 1 in 100); more in males 1.1%; 0.5% in females. This is 66 x the general population risk.
Roughly 1% will die by completed suicide in the 24 months after the initial parasuicidal act, with the risk highest in the weeks following the
original act. This represents mortality by suicide 50-100 times that of the general population. Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 730

questions.question_text: The risk factors for a completed suicide include all except
questions.explanation:
Risk factors for completed suicide socio-demographic factors: male sex, elderly, single, divorced, or widowed, living alone, poor social
support, unemployed or low socio-economic class.  
Personal/mental health factors: previous parasuicide or DSH, any mental disorder (greatest risk in major depression and anorexia nervosa,
then functional psychosis, then neurotic and personality disorders), dependence on alcohol or drugs, recent inpatient psychiatric treatment,
concurrent physical disorder and recent bereavement

questions.question_text: What percentage of people that die by suicide have recognizable psychiatric disorders at the time of death?
questions.explanation: Reports suggest that almost 90% are eligible to be diagnosed as depressed.

questions.question_text: Catatonia refers to increased muscle tone that is

options.text: Present on both active and passive movements
Reduced on both active or passive movement

correct_answer.text: Reduced on both active or passive movement

questions.explanation:
Psychomotor manifestations of catatonia analyzed by latent class techniques have been divided into 4 classes as follows: automatic,
repetitive/echo, withdrawal, and agitated/resistive.

questions.question_text: Which of the following patients is at the highest risk of suicide?

options.text: 44 year old father of 2 children in a heterosexual partnership
35 year old widower, unemployed, social class V
60 year old man, married, social class V
30 year old woman, part-time employed, social class I
16 year old single, unmarried, social class I

correct_answer.text: 60 year old man, married, social class V

questions.explanation: Middle aged men are at a higher risk compared to any other group described

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements with regard to epidemiology of suicides is false?

options.text: Males commit more suicides than females
Females attempt more suicides than males
Across various nations the most common method of suicide remains the same
Diagnosis of any mental disorder increases the suicide risk
Completed suicides are far lesser than attempted suicides

correct_answer.text: Across various nations the most common method of suicide remains the same

questions.explanation:
Method of suicide varies widely depending on availability and access to means. For example, in the US �rearms account for the highest
numbers while poisoning by overdose kills the most in the UK.

questions.question_text:
The most common risk factor for suicide attempts according to the Psychiatric Morbidity Survey conducted by the O�ce of National
Statistics is
questions.explanation: Low socio-economic class (social class 5) is one the most common risk factor for suicide attempts according to Psychiatric morbidity survey

questions.question_text:
Mr X is a 27 year old gentleman who has a well established diagnosis of chronic schizophrenia. He was recently started on a new
antipsychotic medication 2 weeks ago. Today he was brought to the A & E department after his community psychiatric nurse called for an
ambulance. He has a temperature of 104°F and had severe muscular rigidity examination. His pulse rate was raised, blood pressure is
elevated and he has a leucocytosis. He was unable to give a proper history as he appeared to be confused and disorientated. Which of the
following medications is helpful in the pharmacological treatment of this gentleman?
questions.explanation:
In the psychiatric unit; withdraw antipsychotics, monitor temperature, pulse and blood pressure. In the medical unit; Rehydration, sedation
with Benzodiazepines, drugs like Bromocriptine and dandrolene, arti�cial ventilation if required.

questions.question_text:
A 25-year-old man recently returned from a business trip in the United States of America. He presents with aggressive behaviour. He
recently developed seizures and has periods of decreased consciousness. His full blood count, lumbar puncture and liver functions are
normal. Which of the following is a likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
In complex partial seizures, investigations are normal. Decreased periods of consciousness is common. Complex partial seizures begin as
simple partial seizures and progress to impairment of consciousness. There may be also impairment of consciousness at the onset.
Aggressive behaviour is also a possibility in patients with complex partial seizures.

questions.question_text: In which decade was ECT introduced into psychiatric treatment for the �rst time?
questions.explanation: Electroconvulsive therapy was �rst introduced as an e�ective treatment option for psychiatric illness in 1938 by Cerletti and Bini

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is at low risk of developing acute dystonias?

options.text: Patients who are prescribed high potency drugs
Previously neuroleptic naive patients now exposed to antipsychotics
Patients who have been recently started on antipsychotic therapy

questions.explanation:
Dystonia can occur within hours of starting antipsychotics. (Minutes if the IM or IV route is used) and is characterised by muscle spasm in
any part of the body E.g. eye rolling upwards, (oculogyric crisis), head and neck twisted to the side (Torticollis). It can be painful and very
frightening. High risk of developing acute Dystonias: Young males, Neuroleptic naive, and use of high potency drugs such as Haloperidol.

questions.question_text: Considering the epidemiology of suicides which of the following is true?

options.text: During economic recession suicide contributes to lesser global mortality
All industrialized nations have comparable suicide rates
During periods of world war, suicide contributed to greater global mortality
Young adult males have a declining trend in suicide rates

questions.explanation: Due to variable patterns of recording and registering deaths across nations, suicide statistics has low reliability internationally.

questions.question_text:
Which one of the following diagnosis best applies to an 18-year-old girl who suddenly developed akinetic mutism, narrowed consciousness
within few hours? She has no history of previous depression.
questions.explanation:
Dissociative stupor is diagnosed on the basis of a profound diminution or absence of voluntary movement and normal responsiveness to
external stimuli such as light, noise, and touch, but examination and investigation reveal no evidence of a physical cause. In addition, there is
positive evidence of psychogenic causation in the form of recent stressful events or problems according to ICD -10

questions.question_text: Delirium tremens is characterized by onset after
questions.explanation:
Delirium tremens is characterized by onset within 48-72 hours of abstinence, with disturbance worse at night.It is characterized by
hallucinations of multiple modalities.

Refers to a general decision making ability
It may be absent for one task but present for another
Cannot be assessed if patient is psychotic.
Best assessed only by a psychiatrist

correct_answer.text: It may be absent for one task but present for another

questions.explanation: Capacity is time-speci�c and decision speci�c.

questions.question_text: Paul has acute onset auditory hallucinations despite clear consciousness. This is most likely to be caused by:
questions.explanation:
Auditory hallucinations in clear consciousness are seen in alcoholic hallucinosis or stimulant use, apart from schizophrenia and other
functional psychosis. All other listed options will result in some degree of altered level of attention and consciousness (delirium).

questions.question_text: What is the percentage of elderly patients with cognitive impairment that present with sexual disinhibition?
questions.explanation:
As many as 7-25% of seriously cognitively impaired older adults are reported to display sexually inappropriate behaviors. More recent
�gures suggest a narrower index of 10 to 19%. Burns A, Jacoby R, Levy R. Psychiatric phenomenon in Alzheimer's disease. IV: Disorders of
behaviour. Br J Psych 1990;157:86-94.

questions.question_text: The number of people who attend their primary care physician (GP) in the week preceding their suicide is
questions.explanation:
Approximately one-quarter of individuals who complete suicide have been in contact with mental health services. In the week preceding
suicide, 40% of patients make contact with their GPs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a catatonic sign?
questions.explanation: Ambivalence is an inability to make decisions; it is not a catatonic sign on its own unless it manifests as ambitendence.

questions.question_text: In England, the proportion of preventable suicides from a mental healthcare perspective is
questions.explanation:
About 250 suicides (1 in 4) could be prevented each year in the UK, according to the National Con�dential Inquiry into suicide and homicide
by people with mental illness.

questions.question_text: Which among the following psychiatric diagnosis has a higher suicidal risk?
questions.explanation:
A high suicide risk is associated with type 2 bipolar disorder. A recent study suggests that 17% of Bipolar 1 patients, 24% of Bipolar 2 patients
and 12% of Unipolar depressive patients attempt suicide. Bipolar type 2 patients does not only involve higher suicide risk but also a higher
frequency of mood episode, co morbidity and rapid cycling.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factor increases the risk of self harm in �rst episode psychosis?

options.text: Short interval between onset and clinical treatment

questions.explanation:
11.3% of those with �rst episode psychosis engage in self-harm between the onset of psychotic symptoms and �rst presentation to services.
The independent correlates of self-harm were: male gender, belonging to social class I/II, depression and a prolonged period of untreated
psychosis. Increased insight was also associated with risk of self-harm (Harvey 2008 BJPsych 192:178-184).

questions.question_text: Of all causes contributing to global mortality, suicide is responsible for
questions.explanation: 10 to 20 for every 1000 dying globally are due to suicide.

questions.question_text:
With regard to surveys in those with suicidal ideas, the proportion of those who progress from having mere suicidal ideas to plans or
attempts within one year is
questions.explanation:
(Nock et al, The British Journal of Psychiatry (2008) 192: 98-105) According to 17 countries data as a part of WMH survey initiative, the cross-
national lifetime prevalence of suicidal ideation, plans, and attempts is 9.2%, 3.1% and 2.7% . Across all countries, 60% of transitions from
ideation to plan and attempt occur within the �rst year after ideation onset.

questions.question_text: Identify the one, which can be best described as a primary prevention strategy for suicide in old age.

options.text: Treatment of a depressive episode with medications

questions.explanation:
Development of social networks is a primary prevention strategy for suicide in old age. All other options are secondary prevention
strategies.

questions.question_text:
An anxious mother telephones you and asks whether antidepressants will drive her son to suicide. Which of the following is the most
important question that you would ask her?

options.text: Has he attempted suicide in the past?
How many episodes of depression has her son had so far?
Is he living with anyone at home?

questions.explanation:
The risk of suicidal behaviours associated with antidepressants was found to be elevated in subjects under age 25, neutral in subjects aged
25 to 64 (reduced if suicidal behaviour and ideation are considered together), and reduced in subjects aged 65 and older (so protective in
elderly). Tiihonen, J et al. Antidepressants and the Risk of Suicide, Attempted Suicide, and Overall Mortality in a Nationwide Cohort. Arch Gen
Psychiatry. 2006;63:1358-1367.

questions.question_text: The strongest known risk factor for suicide is

options.text: Family history of mental health problems
Past history of mental health problems

questions.explanation: Strongest risk factor of suicide is DSH history.
